feed.title: NPR Topics: Politics
feed.subtitle: Follow NPR Politics for nonpartisan coverage of government, elections, policy debates and voting rights. Plus weekday audio from The NPR Politics Podcast.

entry.title: Nvidia CEO steps down. And, Sen. Chris Van Hollen to run for majority leader
entry.summary: Nvidia's chief financial officer has been appointed interim CEO after Jensen Huang stepped down from the role. And, Sen. Chris Van Hollen says he will challenge Chuck Schumer for majority leader.

entry.title: Hegseth awards medal to soldier who chastised him
entry.summary:
Pete Hegseth was yelled at by a sentinel for poor decorum at Arlington National Cemetery. Now the Secretary of Defense has
given him a medal.

entry.title: These swing voters have low expectations for divided government
entry.summary: Key voters in North Carolina are pessimistic the blue wave flipping control of Congress will solve their economic woes. Many say President Trump will be the chief obstacle.

entry.title: These two voter turnout trends explain what happened across the South in the election
entry.summary: In six states across the Deep South, a drastic swing to the left this election was driven by high Black voter turnout and compounded by a sharp decline in voting rates across Republican-heavy areas.

entry.title: Trump redirects Vance from Iran to focus on combatting fraud in Democratic-led states
entry.summary: President Trump now says there is no need for an Iran deal, pushing Vice President Vance to instead focus on battling corruption.

entry.title: Chris Van Hollen says he will challenge Chuck Schumer for Senate majority leader
entry.summary: Van Hollen, a progressive from Maryland, said voters sent a clear message in the midterm elections — that they want "change from the status quo."

entry.title: Cindy Holscher wins in Kansas, holding governor's office for Democrats
entry.summary: Holscher, a state senator, overcame a more well-known Republican who had Trump's endorsement in the state that has gone to the GOP in most other statewide races.

entry.title: Democrats want to stop Trump's arch, golf course and more. What are their options?
entry.summary: As Trump's arch and other projects make their way through the courts, many critics are looking to Congress to stop them. Democrats have a few tools, including funding and oversight.

entry.title: Witnesses describe the D.C. shooting that left 1 dead, 4 injured
entry.summary: A gunman opened fire at a gym in Washington, D.C.'s Logan Circle Thursday morning. One person has been confirmed killed and four others injured. The gunman is dead, according to police.
